content: Hi, I'm Priya from Alice Corp. Our account ID is AC-77812. Our checkout API started returning errors this morning around 9am IST.
Hi Priya, thanks for reaching out. I'm sorry checkout is affected. Which error code are you seeing, and is it every request or only some of them?
It's error 503 Service Unavailable. Roughly 40% of requests fail. The rest succeed but are slow, about 4 seconds instead of the usual 300ms.
Understood: 503 on about 40% of requests plus high latency on the rest. That usually means the gateway cannot reach enough healthy upstream workers. Which region is your deployment in?
We run in asia-south1 with a failover in europe-west2. Only asia-south1 seems affected.
Thanks. I checked the status page: asia-south1 shows degraded worker health since 08:52 IST. europe-west2 is healthy. Have you deployed anything in the last 24 hours?
Yes, we pushed release 3.14.0 of our checkout service last night at 11pm. It added a new fraud-check call before payment.
That's useful. Does the new fraud-check call go through our gateway too, or directly to a third-party provider?
Through your gateway, to an internal fraud service we also host on your platform.
Then every checkout now makes two gateway calls instead of one, which doubles the load on the asia-south1 worker pool. Your pool is configured for 12 workers. Can you share the worker CPU graph?
CPU on all 12 workers is pinned at 95-100% since 9am. Memory looks fine, around 55%.

That confirms it: the workers are CPU-bound, so health checks time out and the gateway marks them unhealthy, which causes the 503s. Short-term fix: scale the pool to 24 workers with `nwctl workers scale --region asia-south1 --count 24`. Do you have permission to run that?
I don't, only our platform lead Rahul does. He's in a meeting for another hour.

No problem. Two options meanwhile: 1) fail over checkout traffic to europe-west2, which is healthy, or 2) temporarily disable the fraud-check call with your feature flag, if you have one. Which is easier for your team?
We have a feature flag called fraud_check_v2. Disabling it is allowed for me, but our compliance team must approve if it's off for more than 2 hours.
Then disabling fraud_check_v2 now is the fastest fix, as long as Rahul scales the pool within 2 hours. Please turn the flag off and tell me what you see.
Done. Flag is off since 10:41 IST. Error rate dropped to about 2% and latency is back to 350ms.

Great news, that confirms the root cause. Remaining 2% errors are likely workers still recovering; they should clear within 10 minutes. I've opened incident INC-20931 to track this. Next step: Rahul scales to 24 workers, then you re-enable the flag.
Thanks. Will scaling to 24 workers change our bill?

Yes. On your Enterprise plan each extra worker costs $0.42 per hour, so 12 extra workers add about $5 per hour, roughly $3,630 per month if left on. You can enable autoscaling (min 12, max 24) so you only pay for the extra workers during peaks.
Autoscaling sounds better. Can it react fast enough for flash sales? We have a big sale on Friday at 8pm.

Autoscaling adds workers within about 90 seconds of CPU passing 70%. For a planned flash sale, I recommend scheduling a pre-scale to 24 workers at 7:30pm Friday with `nwctl workers schedule`, then letting autoscaling handle the rest.
Perfect. One more thing: our finance team asked if this outage qualifies for an SLA credit.

Your SLA covers platform-caused unavailability. Here the trigger was extra load from your release, so the 503s themselves likely do not qualify. However, the status page showed degraded health starting 08:52, before your traffic peak, so I've asked our SRE team to review. You'll get an answer on INC-20931 within 3 business days.
Okay. Rahul just came out of his meeting and scaled the pool to 24 workers. CPU is now around 48%.
Excellent. With CPU at 48% you have plenty of headroom. You can now re-enable fraud_check_v2 safely. Please watch error rate for 15 minutes after turning it back on.
Flag is back on since 11:52 IST. Error rate is 0.1% and latency is 320ms. All good.

That's a full recovery. Summary of next steps: 1) set up autoscaling min 12 / max 24, 2) schedule the pre-scale for Friday 7:30pm, 3) wait for the SRE review on the SLA credit in INC-20931. Is there anything else I can help with?
